source.text: וְיִפְתָּ֣ח הַגִּלְעָדִ֗י הָיָה֙ גִּבּ֣וֹר חַ֔יִל וְה֖וּא בֶּן־אִשָּׁ֣ה זוֹנָ֑ה וַיּ֥וֹלֶד גִּלְעָ֖ד אֶת־יִפְתָּֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: And Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty [man] of strength, and he [was the] son of a woman, a prostitute; and fathered Gilead Jephthah.

en.L: And Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of strength, and he [was the] son of a woman [who was] a prostitute; and Gilead fathered Jephthah.
en.B: Jephthah the Gileadite was a strong warrior. He was the son of a prostitute, and his father was Gilead.
en.R: Jephthah from Gilead was a brave and strong fighter. His mother was a prostitute, and his father was a man named Gilead.

sw.L: Naye Yeftha Mgileadi alikuwa shujaa hodari wa vita, naye [alikuwa] mwana wa mwanamke kahaba; naye Gileadi akamzaa Yeftha.
sw.B: Yeftha Mgileadi alikuwa shujaa hodari wa vita. Alikuwa mwana wa kahaba, na baba yake alikuwa Gileadi.
sw.R: Yeftha wa Gileadi alikuwa mpiganaji jasiri na mwenye nguvu. Mama yake alikuwa kahaba, na baba yake alikuwa mtu aitwaye Gileadi.

es.L: Y Jefté el galaadita era un hombre valiente y fuerte, y él [era] hijo de una mujer [que era] prostituta; y Galaad engendró a Jefté.
es.B: Jefté el galaadita era un guerrero valiente. Era hijo de una prostituta, y su padre era Galaad.
es.R: Jefté, de Galaad, era un luchador valiente y fuerte. Su madre era una prostituta, y su padre era un hombre llamado Galaad.

decisions.choice: a mighty man of strength: a proven fighting man
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Gideon (6:12) and of men able to fight (2 Kings 24:14). It names a man known for courage and skill in war; it may also suggest a man of some standing, but here the story makes him a fighter first.

decisions.choice: son of a woman, a prostitute: born outside his father's marriage
decisions.reason: Jephthah's mother was not Gilead's wife but a prostitute. This gives him no rightful place in the family, as the next verse shows, and it puts him among the unlikely leaders the book tells of.

decisions.choice: Gilead fathered Jephthah: a man named Gilead
decisions.reason: Gilead is also the name of the region and of a clan of Manasseh (Numbers 26:29). Here it names Jephthah's father. The name may show how closely the man and his family belonged to the land and people of Gilead.

decisions.choice: a man named Gilead
decisions.reason: Readable adds "a man named" so the reader does not confuse the father with the region of Gilead in the same sentence.

decisions.choice: "Yeftha" for Jephthah; "Mgileadi" (a man of Gilead) at Literal and Balanced, "wa Gileadi" at Readable
decisions.reason: "Yeftha" is the form already used in Hebrews 11:32, so the Old Testament story and the New Testament list name him alike. "Mgileadi" is the usual Swahili way to name a man by his people (as "Mwamori"); Readable says "of Gilead", the plainer phrase.

decisions.choice: "Jefté", "el galaadita", "Galaad"; and the other names of these chapters in their usual Spanish forms (Sijón, Hesbón, Jahaz, el Arnón, el Jaboc, Quemos, Mizpa)
decisions.reason: For Judges 11-21: Jephthah is "Jefté", the form Spanish already uses in Hebrews 11:32; the region and the man are "Galaad", as in Deuteronomy, and the other names follow the forms used in Numbers and Deuteronomy.

source.text: וַתֵּ֧לֶד אֵֽשֶׁת־גִּלְעָ֛ד ל֖וֹ בָּנִ֑ים וַיִּגְדְּל֨וּ בְֽנֵי־הָאִשָּׁ֜ה וַיְגָרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־יִפְתָּ֗ח וַיֹּ֤אמְרוּ לוֹ֙ לֹֽא־תִנְחַ֣ל בְּבֵית־אָבִ֔ינוּ כִּ֛י בֶּן־אִשָּׁ֥ה אַחֶ֖רֶת אָֽתָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And bore the wife of Gilead to him sons, and grew up the sons of the wife, and they drove out Jephthah and said to him, not you will inherit in [the] house of our father, for [the] son of a woman another [are] you.

en.L: And the wife of Gilead bore him sons, and the sons of the wife grew up, and they drove Jephthah out and said to him, "You will not inherit in the house of our father, for you [are the] son of another woman."
en.B: Gilead's wife also bore him sons. When they grew up, they drove Jephthah away and told him, "You will have no share in our father's estate, because you are the son of another woman."
en.R: Gilead's wife had sons too. When they grew up, they forced Jephthah to leave. They said, "You will not get any of our father's property. You are the son of a different woman."

sw.L: Naye mke wa Gileadi akamzalia wana; nao wana wa mke huyo wakakua, wakamfukuza Yeftha, wakamwambia, "Hutarithi katika nyumba ya baba yetu, kwa maana wewe [ni] mwana wa mwanamke mwingine."
sw.B: Mke wa Gileadi naye alimzalia wana. Walipokua, walimfukuza Yeftha, wakamwambia, "Hutapata sehemu yoyote ya mali ya baba yetu, kwa sababu wewe ni mwana wa mwanamke mwingine."
sw.R: Mke wa Gileadi pia alizaa wana. Walipokuwa wakubwa, walimlazimisha Yeftha aondoke. Walisema, "Hutapata chochote katika mali ya baba yetu. Wewe ni mwana wa mwanamke mwingine."

es.L: Y la mujer de Galaad le dio a luz hijos, y los hijos de la mujer crecieron, y echaron a Jefté y le dijeron: «Tú no heredarás en la casa de nuestro padre, porque [eres] hijo de otra mujer».
es.B: La esposa de Galaad también le dio hijos. Cuando crecieron, echaron a Jefté y le dijeron: «Tú no tendrás parte en la herencia de nuestro padre, porque eres hijo de otra mujer».
es.R: La esposa de Galaad también tuvo hijos. Cuando crecieron, obligaron a Jefté a irse. Le dijeron: «No recibirás nada de los bienes de nuestro padre. Tú eres hijo de otra mujer».

decisions.choice: not inherit in our father's house: no share in the family's land and goods
decisions.reason: The "house of our father" is the family and what it owns. The sons of Gilead's wife shut out the son of the prostitute from any share. The law protected a firstborn son of a less loved wife (Deuteronomy 21:15-17), but a prostitute's son had no such claim; Sarah similarly wanted Hagar's son shut out of the inheritance (Genesis 21:10).

decisions.choice: drove out: forced him to leave by pressure or force
decisions.reason: The verb is used of driving people out of a place they had lived in. Jephthah later says the elders of Gilead shared in this (verse 7).

decisions.choice: our father's estate / our father's property
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "inherit in the house of our father" means; Literal keeps the phrase.

source.text: וַיִּבְרַ֤ח יִפְתָּח֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י אֶחָ֔יו וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּאֶ֣רֶץ ט֑וֹב וַיִּֽתְלַקְּט֤וּ אֶל־יִפְתָּח֙ אֲנָשִׁ֣ים רֵיקִ֔ים וַיֵּצְא֖וּ עִמּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And fled Jephthah from [the] face of his brothers and dwelt in [the] land of Tob; and gathered themselves to Jephthah men empty, and they went out with him.

en.L: And Jephthah fled from the presence of his brothers and lived in the land of Tob; and empty men gathered themselves to Jephthah, and they went out with him.
en.B: So Jephthah escaped from his brothers and made his home in the land of Tob. A band of worthless men gathered around him and went out raiding with him.
en.R: So Jephthah ran away from his brothers and went to live in the land of Tob. A gang of rough men with nothing to lose joined him, and they went out on raids together.

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akakimbia kutoka mbele ya ndugu zake, akakaa katika nchi ya Tobu; na watu wasio na kitu wakajikusanya kwa Yeftha, nao wakatoka pamoja naye.
sw.B: Basi Yeftha aliwakimbia ndugu zake, akaishi katika nchi ya Tobu. Kundi la watu wasiofaa kitu likakusanyika kumzunguka, nao wakatoka pamoja naye kwenda kuvamia.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Yeftha aliwakimbia ndugu zake, akaenda kuishi katika nchi ya Tobu. Genge la watu wakorofi wasio na cha kupoteza lilijiunga naye, nao wakawa wakitoka pamoja kwenda kuvamia.

es.L: Y Jefté huyó de la presencia de sus hermanos y habitó en la tierra de Tob; y se juntaron con Jefté hombres vacíos, y salían con él.
es.B: Así que Jefté huyó de sus hermanos y se estableció en la tierra de Tob. Se le juntó una banda de hombres sin oficio ni beneficio, que salían con él a hacer incursiones.
es.R: Entonces Jefté se escapó de sus hermanos y se fue a vivir a la tierra de Tob. Allí se le unió un grupo de hombres rudos que no tenían nada que perder, y salían juntos a atacar y saquear.

decisions.choice: the land of Tob: a region north and east of Gilead
decisions.reason: Tob lay beyond Israel's settled land, toward Aram. Later the Ammonites hire men from Tob against David (2 Samuel 10:6, 8).

decisions.choice: empty men: men without land, means or standing
decisions.reason: "Empty" men are men with nothing to their name, ready for any risk. Abimelech hired the same kind of men (9:4), and David later gathers a similar band (1 Samuel 22:2).

decisions.choice: went out with him: went out on raids
decisions.reason: "Go out" is often used of going out to fight. With a band of such men, it most likely means raiding, which explains how Jephthah gained the fighting skill the elders want.

decisions.choice: went out raiding / went out on raids
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the most likely sense of "went out" (m3). Literal keeps the bare verb.

decisions.choice: "hombres vacíos" (L); "hombres sin oficio ni beneficio" (B); "hombres rudos que no tenían nada que perder" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of "empty" men; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m2): men with no land, means or standing. "Sin oficio ni beneficio" is the everyday Spanish phrase for that.

source.text: וַיְהִ֖י מִיָּמִ֑ים וַיִּלָּחֲמ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֖וֹן עִם־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after days, and fought [the] sons of Ammon with Israel.

en.L: And it was after [some] days, and the sons of Ammon fought with Israel.
en.B: Some time later the Ammonites went to war against Israel.
en.R: After some time, the Ammonites started a war against Israel.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya siku [kadhaa], wana wa Amoni wakapigana na Israeli.
sw.B: Baada ya muda Waamoni walikwenda kupigana vita dhidi ya Israeli.
sw.R: Baada ya muda, Waamoni walianzisha vita dhidi ya Israeli.

es.L: Y sucedió después de [algunos] días, que los hijos de Amón hicieron guerra contra Israel.
es.B: Algún tiempo después, los amonitas declararon la guerra a Israel.
es.R: Después de un tiempo, los amonitas comenzaron una guerra contra Israel.

decisions.choice: after days: after some time
decisions.reason: The phrase sets no exact length of time. The story goes back to the war already begun in 10:17.

decisions.choice: "wana wa Amoni" at Literal; "Waamoni" at Balanced and Readable; likewise "wana wa Israeli" (L) and "Waisraeli" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: For this block, as the Pentateuch drafts do for Israel: Literal keeps the Hebrew "sons of", and "wana" already means children of either sex; Balanced and Readable use the people's name. Swahili has no second wording for the gender setting to change.

source.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁר־נִלְחֲמ֥וּ בְנֵֽי־עַמּ֖וֹן עִם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ זִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד לָקַ֥חַת אֶת־יִפְתָּ֖ח מֵאֶ֥רֶץ טֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when fought [the] sons of Ammon with Israel, and went [the] elders of Gilead to fetch Jephthah from [the] land of Tob.

en.L: And it was, when the sons of Ammon fought with Israel, that the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob.
en.B: When the Ammonites were fighting against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob.
en.R: So while the Ammonites were at war with Israel, the leaders of Gilead went to the land of Tob to get Jephthah.

sw.L: Ikawa wana wa Amoni walipopigana na Israeli, wazee wa Gileadi wakaenda kumleta Yeftha kutoka nchi ya Tobu.
sw.B: Waamoni walipokuwa wakipigana na Israeli, wazee wa Gileadi walikwenda kumrudisha Yeftha kutoka nchi ya Tobu.
sw.R: Basi Waamoni walipokuwa wakipigana na Israeli, viongozi wa Gileadi walikwenda katika nchi ya Tobu kumchukua Yeftha.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando los hijos de Amón hicieron guerra contra Israel, los ancianos de Galaad fueron a traer a Jefté de la tierra de Tob.
es.B: Mientras los amonitas peleaban contra Israel, los ancianos de Galaad fueron a buscar a Jefté a la tierra de Tob.
es.R: Así que, mientras los amonitas estaban en guerra con Israel, los líderes de Galaad fueron a la tierra de Tob a buscar a Jefté.

decisions.choice: the elders of Gilead: the heads of the families and towns of the region
decisions.reason: Elders were the older men who led families and towns and spoke for them. These are the leaders who had asked who would lead the fight against Ammon (10:18).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says "leaders" for "elders" here, because the point is their office, not their age.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לְיִפְתָּ֔ח לְכָ֕ה וְהָיִ֥יתָה לָּ֖נוּ לְקָצִ֑ין וְנִֽלָּחֲמָ֖ה בִּבְנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they said to Jephthah, come and be to us for commander, and let us fight against [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: And they said to Jephthah, "Come and be our commander, and let us fight against the sons of Ammon."
en.B: They said to Jephthah, "Come and be our commander, so that we can fight the Ammonites."
en.R: They said to Jephthah, "Come and lead our army, so that we can fight the Ammonites."

sw.L: Wakamwambia Yeftha, "Njoo uwe kamanda wetu, nasi tupigane na wana wa Amoni."
sw.B: Walimwambia Yeftha, "Njoo uwe kamanda wetu, ili tuweze kupigana na Waamoni."
sw.R: Walimwambia Yeftha, "Njoo uliongoze jeshi letu, ili tuweze kupigana na Waamoni."

es.L: Y dijeron a Jefté: «Ven y sé nuestro jefe, y pelearemos contra los hijos de Amón».
es.B: Le dijeron a Jefté: «Ven y sé nuestro jefe, para que podamos pelear contra los amonitas».
es.R: Le dijeron a Jefté: «Ven y dirige nuestro ejército, para que podamos pelear contra los amonitas».

decisions.choice: commander: a leader in war only
decisions.reason: The word names a military chief. The elders first offer Jephthah command of the army for this war. In verse 8 they raise the offer to "head" over all the people of Gilead, and in verse 11 he is made both.

decisions.choice: let us fight: so that we may fight
decisions.reason: The verb expresses what the elders want to do once Jephthah leads them; it gives the purpose of their request.

decisions.choice: lead our army
decisions.reason: Readable says what a commander does, so the step up to "head" in verse 8 stays clear.

decisions.choice: "tú" for one person addressed ("ven", "sé"); "ustedes" forms by default for several, with the plural-you setting giving "vosotros" (verse 7)
decisions.reason: For Judges 11-21 and as in the Pentateuch: a single person is addressed with "tú"; wherever several people are addressed, Spanish must choose a plural form, and the default is the "ustedes" form most Spanish speakers use, with the "vosotros" form of Spain as the reader setting. The span covers each verb, pronoun or possessive that changes.

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יִפְתָּח֙ לְזִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד הֲלֹ֤א אַתֶּם֙ שְׂנֵאתֶ֣ם אוֹתִ֔י וַתְּגָרְשׁ֖וּנִי מִבֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וּמַדּ֜וּעַ בָּאתֶ֤ם אֵלַי֙ עַ֔תָּה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צַ֥ר לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jephthah to [the] elders of Gilead, [did] not you hate me and drive me out from [the] house of my father? And why have you come to me now, when distress [is] to you?

en.L: And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Did you not hate me and drive me out of the house of my father? And why have you come to me now, when you are in distress?"
en.B: But Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Was it not you who hated me and drove me out of my father's house? Why come to me now, when you are in trouble?"
en.R: But Jephthah answered the leaders of Gilead, "You hated me and forced me to leave my father's home! So why are you coming to me now that you are in trouble?"

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akawaambia wazee wa Gileadi, "Je, si ninyi mlionichukia na kunifukuza kutoka nyumba ya baba yangu? Basi kwa nini mmenijia sasa, mnapokuwa katika dhiki?"
sw.B: Lakini Yeftha aliwaambia wazee wa Gileadi, "Je, si ninyi mlionichukia mkanifukuza kutoka nyumbani kwa baba yangu? Kwa nini mnanijia sasa, mnapokuwa katika taabu?"
sw.R: Lakini Yeftha aliwajibu viongozi wa Gileadi, "Ninyi mlinichukia na kunilazimisha niondoke nyumbani kwa baba yangu! Basi kwa nini mnakuja kwangu sasa kwa kuwa mko katika taabu?"

es.L: Y Jefté dijo a los ancianos de Galaad: «¿No me {{plural_you:odiaron ustedes|odiasteis vosotros}} y me {{plural_you:echaron|echasteis}} de la casa de mi padre? ¿Y por qué {{plural_you:vienen|venís}} a mí ahora, cuando {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en apuros?».
es.B: Pero Jefté respondió a los ancianos de Galaad: «¿No fueron {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} los que me odiaron y me echaron de la casa de mi padre? ¿Por qué {{plural_you:vienen|venís}} a mí ahora, cuando {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en apuros?».
es.R: Pero Jefté les contestó a los líderes de Galaad: «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} me odiaban y me obligaron a irme de la casa de mi padre! ¿Por qué {{plural_you:vienen|venís}} a buscarme ahora que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} en problemas?».

decisions.choice: did not you hate me: a question that accuses
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes. The pronoun "you" is stressed: Jephthah lays the blame on the elders themselves, not only on his brothers, perhaps because they supported or allowed his expulsion.

decisions.choice: when distress is to you: only now that you need me
decisions.reason: Jephthah points out that they turn to him only in need. The LORD had said much the same to Israel in 10:13-14: you left me, so cry to the gods you chose. Jephthah's bargaining follows.

decisions.choice: statement with an exclamation mark
decisions.reason: Readable turns the first question into the statement it implies, so its force is not missed.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ זִקְנֵ֨י גִלְעָ֜ד אֶל־יִפְתָּ֗ח לָכֵן֙ עַתָּה֙ שַׁ֣בְנוּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְהָלַכְתָּ֣ עִמָּ֔נוּ וְנִלְחַמְתָּ֖ בִּבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וְהָיִ֤יתָ לָּ֨נוּ֙ לְרֹ֔אשׁ לְכֹ֖ל יֹשְׁבֵ֥י גִלְעָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] elders of Gilead to Jephthah, therefore now we have returned to you, and you will go with us and fight against [the] sons of Ammon, and you will be to us for head of all [the] inhabitants of Gilead.

en.L: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "That is why we have now come back to you: you will go with us and fight against the sons of Ammon, and you will be head over us, over all the inhabitants of Gilead."
en.B: The elders of Gilead answered Jephthah, "That is exactly why we have come back to you now. Come with us and fight the Ammonites, and you will be our head, ruling over everyone who lives in Gilead."
en.R: The leaders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "Yes, that is why we have come back to you now. Come with us and fight the Ammonites. Then you will be the ruler over all of us who live in Gilead."

sw.L: Nao wazee wa Gileadi wakamwambia Yeftha, "Ndiyo sababu sasa tumerudi kwako: utakwenda pamoja nasi na kupigana na wana wa Amoni, nawe utakuwa kichwa juu yetu, juu ya wakaaji wote wa Gileadi."
sw.B: Wazee wa Gileadi walimjibu Yeftha, "Hiyo ndiyo sababu hasa tumerudi kwako sasa. Njoo pamoja nasi upigane na Waamoni, nawe utakuwa mkuu wetu, mtawala wa wote wanaoishi Gileadi."
sw.R: Viongozi wa Gileadi walimwambia Yeftha, "Ndiyo, hiyo ndiyo sababu tumerudi kwako sasa. Njoo pamoja nasi upigane na Waamoni. Kisha utakuwa mtawala juu yetu sote tunaoishi Gileadi."

es.L: Y los ancianos de Galaad dijeron a Jefté: «Por eso ahora hemos vuelto a ti: irás con nosotros y pelearás contra los hijos de Amón, y serás nuestra cabeza, de todos los habitantes de Galaad».
es.B: Los ancianos de Galaad le respondieron a Jefté: «Precisamente por eso hemos vuelto ahora a ti. Ven con nosotros y pelea contra los amonitas, y serás nuestro jefe y gobernarás a todos los que viven en Galaad».
es.R: Los líderes de Galaad le dijeron a Jefté: «Sí, por eso hemos vuelto a buscarte. Ven con nosotros y pelea contra los amonitas. Después serás el gobernante de todos los que vivimos en Galaad».

decisions.choice: therefore: that is why, because we are in distress
decisions.reason: The word picks up Jephthah's complaint and turns it: yes, it is because of the trouble that we have come. It does not deny what he said about the past.

decisions.choice: head of all the inhabitants of Gilead: ruler of the whole region
decisions.reason: "Head" is more than "commander" (verse 6): it means lasting rule over all Gilead, not only command in this war. It is what the leaders had promised in 10:18 to whoever began the fight against Ammon.

decisions.choice: Come with us
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and you will go with us" sets out the terms; Balanced and Readable put it as an invitation, which is how it works in the talk.

decisions.choice: "cabeza" (L); "jefe" (B); "gobernante" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "head"; Balanced and Readable say "jefe" and "gobernante", the ruler of the whole region (m2). The commander of verse 6 (a leader in war only) is "jefe" with "de [nuestro] ejército" understood, so Readable there says "dirige nuestro ejército".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יִפְתָּ֜ח אֶל־זִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֗ד אִם־מְשִׁיבִ֨ים אַתֶּ֤ם אוֹתִי֙ לְהִלָּחֵם֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן וְנָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אוֹתָ֖ם לְפָנָ֑י אָנֹכִ֕י אֶהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לְרֹֽאשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Jephthah to [the] elders of Gilead, if bringing back you me to fight against [the] sons of Ammon, and gives Yahweh them before me, I will be to you for head.

en.L: And Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you bring me back to fight against the sons of Ammon, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives them up before me, I will be your head."
en.B: Jephthah answered the elders of Gilead, "If you bring me back to make war on the Ammonites and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} hands them over to me, then I will be your head."
en.R: Jephthah said to the leaders of Gilead, "Suppose you take me back to fight the Ammonites, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lets me defeat them. Then I will be your ruler. Agreed?"

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akawaambia wazee wa Gileadi, "Kama mkinirudisha nipigane na wana wa Amoni, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatoa mbele yangu, mimi nitakuwa kichwa chenu."
sw.B: Yeftha aliwajibu wazee wa Gileadi, "Mkinirudisha nikapigane vita na Waamoni, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia mikononi mwangu, basi nitakuwa mkuu wenu."
sw.R: Yeftha aliwaambia viongozi wa Gileadi, "Tuseme mnanirudisha nikapigane na Waamoni, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ananiwezesha kuwashinda. Hapo nitakuwa mtawala wenu. Mmekubali?"

es.L: Y Jefté dijo a los ancianos de Galaad: «Si {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} volver para pelear contra los hijos de Amón, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entrega delante de mí, yo seré su cabeza».
es.B: Jefté respondió a los ancianos de Galaad: «Si me {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}} volver para combatir contra los amonitas y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me los entrega, entonces yo seré {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} jefe».
es.R: Jefté les dijo a los líderes de Galaad: «Supongamos que me {{plural_you:llevan|lleváis}} de vuelta para pelear contra los amonitas, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me deja vencerlos. Entonces yo seré {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} gobernante. ¿De acuerdo?».

decisions.choice: I will be your head: a condition set as a statement
decisions.reason: Jephthah restates the elders' offer as his own terms, with the pronoun "I" stressed. The words could also be read as a question ("will I really be your head?"), but either way he wants the promise made firm, as the elders do in verse 10.

decisions.choice: the LORD gives them before me: victory comes from the LORD
decisions.reason: Jephthah speaks of victory as the LORD's gift, as the book does throughout (3:10; 4:14; 7:9). He names the LORD as the one who decides the war, before any vow is made.

decisions.choice: Agreed?
decisions.reason: Readable adds "Agreed?" to show that Jephthah is pinning the elders down, which their oath in verse 10 answers. It is a stretch beyond the words.

decisions.choice: the divine name as "BWANA" in capitals by default, with "Yahwe" as the reader setting
decisions.reason: As in the Pentateuch and Joshua: "BWANA" in capitals, like the English "the LORD", shows that the name itself stands in the Hebrew; "Yahwe" is the alternative for readers who want the name. "Yehova" is a later hybrid form, and plain "Bwana" would hide that the name is used.

decisions.choice: "el SEÑOR" by default, "Yahvé" with the divine name setting ("El SEÑOR" at a sentence start, "del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé")
decisions.reason: For Judges 11-21, as in the Pentateuch: the divine name is "el SEÑOR" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", and the divine name setting gives "Yahvé". The span takes in the article and its contraction so both options read naturally.

source.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ זִקְנֵֽי־גִלְעָ֖ד אֶל־יִפְתָּ֑ח יְהוָ֗ה יִהְיֶ֤ה שֹׁמֵ֨עַ֙ בֵּֽינוֹתֵ֔ינוּ אִם־לֹ֥א כִדְבָרְךָ֖ כֵּ֥ן נַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] elders of Gilead to Jephthah, Yahweh will be hearing between us, if not according to your word so we do.

en.L: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be the one who hears between us, if we do not do just as you say."
en.B: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is witness between us. We will certainly do as you say."
en.R: The leaders of Gilead answered, "{{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is listening and is our witness. We promise to do just what you have said."

sw.L: Nao wazee wa Gileadi wakamwambia Yeftha, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atakuwa msikilizaji kati yetu, ikiwa hatutafanya sawasawa na neno lako."
sw.B: Wazee wa Gileadi walimwambia Yeftha, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ni shahidi kati yetu. Hakika tutafanya kama ulivyosema."
sw.R: Viongozi wa Gileadi walijibu, "{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anasikiliza, naye ni shahidi wetu. Tunaahidi kufanya kama ulivyosema."

es.L: Y los ancianos de Galaad dijeron a Jefté: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} será el que oye entre nosotros, si no hacemos conforme a tu palabra».
es.B: Los ancianos de Galaad le dijeron a Jefté: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es testigo entre nosotros. Haremos sin falta lo que dices».
es.R: Los líderes de Galaad le respondieron: «{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nos está escuchando y es nuestro testigo. Prometemos hacer exactamente lo que has dicho».

decisions.choice: the LORD will be the one hearing between us: the LORD is witness to this agreement
decisions.reason: The elders call on the LORD to hear their promise and hold them to it. Laban uses a similar oath with Jacob (Genesis 31:49-50).

decisions.choice: if we do not do according to your word: a solemn oath, meaning we will surely do it
decisions.reason: An oath in Hebrew often begins "if ..." and leaves the curse unspoken: may the LORD act against us if we fail. It amounts to a firm promise.

decisions.choice: We will certainly do as you say / We promise to do
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the oath form "if we do not do" into the promise it makes (m2).

source.text: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ יִפְתָּח֙ עִם־זִקְנֵ֣י גִלְעָ֔ד וַיָּשִׂ֨ימוּ הָעָ֥ם אוֹת֛וֹ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לְרֹ֣אשׁ וּלְקָצִ֑ין וַיְדַבֵּ֨ר יִפְתָּ֧ח אֶת־כָּל־דְּבָרָ֛יו לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה בַּמִּצְפָּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went Jephthah with [the] elders of Gilead, and made the people him over them for head and for commander; and spoke Jephthah all his words before Yahweh in Mizpah.

en.L: And Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head over them and commander; and Jephthah spoke all his words before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in Mizpah.
en.B: So Jephthah went back with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over themselves as head and commander. And Jephthah repeated all his terms before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at Mizpah.
en.R: So Jephthah went back with the leaders of Gilead. The people made him their ruler and the commander of their army. Then at Mizpah, Jephthah repeated everything he had agreed to, there in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akaenda pamoja na wazee wa Gileadi, na watu wakamweka juu yao kuwa kichwa na kamanda; naye Yeftha akanena maneno yake yote mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} huko Mizpa.
sw.B: Basi Yeftha alirudi pamoja na wazee wa Gileadi, na watu wakamweka juu yao kuwa mkuu na kamanda. Naye Yeftha akayarudia masharti yake yote mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} huko Mizpa.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Yeftha alirudi pamoja na viongozi wa Gileadi. Watu walimfanya kuwa mtawala wao na kamanda wa jeshi lao. Kisha huko Mizpa, Yeftha aliyarudia yote aliyokuwa amekubali, mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

es.L: Y Jefté fue con los ancianos de Galaad, y el pueblo lo puso sobre ellos como cabeza y como jefe; y Jefté habló todas sus palabras delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en Mizpa.
es.B: Así que Jefté volvió con los ancianos de Galaad, y el pueblo lo puso al frente como jefe y comandante. Y Jefté repitió todas sus condiciones delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en Mizpa.
es.R: Entonces Jefté volvió con los líderes de Galaad. El pueblo lo nombró su gobernante y comandante de su ejército. Después, en Mizpa, Jefté repitió todo lo que había acordado, allí en presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: head and commander: both offers given together
decisions.reason: The people give Jephthah both titles: lasting rule (verse 8) and command in war (verse 6).

decisions.choice: spoke all his words before the LORD: the agreement made binding at a place of worship
decisions.reason: Speaking the terms "before the LORD" made the agreement a sacred one, with the LORD as witness (verse 10). Mizpah in Gilead was where Israel had gathered against Ammon (10:17).

decisions.choice: repeated all his terms / repeated everything he had agreed to
decisions.reason: "All his words" here are the terms just agreed; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִפְתָּח֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בְּנֵֽי־עַמּ֖וֹן לֵאמֹ֑ר מַה־לִּ֣י וָלָ֔ךְ כִּֽי־בָ֥אתָ אֵלַ֖י לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם בְּאַרְצִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Jephthah messengers to [the] king of [the] sons of Ammon, saying, what [is] to me and to you, that you have come to me to fight against my land?

en.L: And Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon, saying, "What [is there] between me and you, that you have come to me to fight against my land?"
en.B: Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites with this question: "What quarrel do you have with me, that you have come to attack my land?"
en.R: Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites. They asked him, "What do you have against me? Why have you come to attack my country?"

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akatuma wajumbe kwa mfalme wa wana wa Amoni, akisema, "Kuna [nini] kati yangu na wewe, hata umenijia kupigana na nchi yangu?"
sw.B: Kisha Yeftha alituma wajumbe kwa mfalme wa Waamoni na swali hili: "Una ugomvi gani nami, hata umekuja kuishambulia nchi yangu?"
sw.R: Kisha Yeftha alituma wajumbe kwa mfalme wa Waamoni. Walimwuliza, "Una nini dhidi yangu? Kwa nini umekuja kuishambulia nchi yangu?"

es.L: Y Jefté envió mensajeros al rey de los hijos de Amón, diciendo: «¿Qué [hay] entre tú y yo, que has venido a mí para pelear contra mi tierra?».
es.B: Entonces Jefté envió mensajeros al rey de los amonitas con esta pregunta: «¿Qué tienes contra mí, para que hayas venido a atacar mi tierra?».
es.R: Entonces Jefté envió mensajeros al rey de los amonitas. Le preguntaron: «¿Qué tienes contra mí? ¿Por qué has venido a atacar mi país?».

decisions.choice: what is to me and to you?: what quarrel is there between us?
decisions.reason: The phrase asks what claim one side has on the other. Here it challenges the king to give a reason for his war (compare 2 Samuel 16:10; 1 Kings 17:18).

decisions.choice: my land: Jephthah speaks for Israel
decisions.reason: As head of Gilead, Jephthah speaks of Israel's land as his own, just as the king calls the disputed land "my land" (verse 13). The talks are between two rulers on behalf of their peoples.

decisions.choice: two questions
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question into two short ones.

source.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בְּנֵי־עַמּ֜וֹן אֶל־מַלְאֲכֵ֣י יִפְתָּ֗ח כִּֽי־לָקַ֨ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל אֶת־אַרְצִי֙ בַּעֲלוֹת֣וֹ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם מֵאַרְנ֥וֹן וְעַד־הַיַּבֹּ֖ק וְעַד־הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וְעַתָּ֕ה הָשִׁ֥יבָה אֶתְהֶ֖ן בְּשָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] king of [the] sons of Ammon to [the] messengers of Jephthah, because took Israel my land when it came up from Egypt, from Arnon and to the Jabbok and to the Jordan; and now restore them in peace.

en.L: And the king of the sons of Ammon said to the messengers of Jephthah, "Because Israel took my land when it came up from Egypt, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and to the Jordan. And now give them back in peace."
en.B: The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah's messengers, "Because Israel took my land when they came up from Egypt, all the way from the Arnon to the Jabbok and to the Jordan. Now give it back peacefully."
en.R: The king of the Ammonites gave this answer to Jephthah's messengers: "When the Israelites came up out of Egypt, they took my land. It stretched from the Arnon River north to the Jabbok River and west to the Jordan River. Now give it back to me without a fight."

sw.L: Naye mfalme wa wana wa Amoni akawaambia wajumbe wa Yeftha, "Kwa sababu Israeli aliichukua nchi yangu alipopanda kutoka Misri, kutoka Arnoni hadi Yaboki na hadi Yordani. Basi sasa uzirudishe kwa amani."
sw.B: Mfalme wa Waamoni aliwajibu wajumbe wa Yeftha, "Ni kwa sababu Israeli waliichukua nchi yangu walipopanda kutoka Misri, tangu Arnoni mpaka Yaboki na mpaka Yordani. Sasa uirudishe kwa amani."
sw.R: Mfalme wa Waamoni aliwapa wajumbe wa Yeftha jibu hili: "Waisraeli walipotoka Misri, waliichukua nchi yangu. Ilienea kutoka Mto Arnoni kaskazini hadi Mto Yaboki, na magharibi hadi Mto Yordani. Sasa nirudishie bila vita."

es.L: Y el rey de los hijos de Amón dijo a los mensajeros de Jefté: «Porque Israel tomó mi tierra cuando subió de Egipto, desde el Arnón hasta el Jaboc y hasta el Jordán. Y ahora devuélvelas en paz».
es.B: El rey de los amonitas respondió a los mensajeros de Jefté: «Porque Israel se apoderó de mi tierra cuando subió de Egipto, desde el Arnón hasta el Jaboc y el Jordán. Ahora devuélvemela en paz».
es.R: El rey de los amonitas les dio esta respuesta a los mensajeros de Jefté: «Cuando los israelitas salieron de Egipto, me quitaron mi tierra. Iba desde el río Arnón, al norte hasta el río Jaboc, y al oeste hasta el río Jordán. Ahora devuélvemela sin pelear».

decisions.choice: from the Arnon to the Jabbok and to the Jordan: the land Israel took from Sihon
decisions.reason: These are the bounds of the land Israel took from Sihon king of the Amorites (Numbers 21:24; verse 22 below). The king of Ammon claims it as his own. Numbers says Ammon's border lay beyond it to the east (Numbers 21:24).

decisions.choice: restore them: give back the lands, or the towns in them
decisions.reason: The word "them" is plural, though "land" is singular. It probably means the lands or towns within the bounds just named. The sense is the same: give back the whole area.

decisions.choice: in peace: without war
decisions.reason: The king offers to stop the war if the land is handed over. The words are a demand, not a request.

decisions.choice: it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "it" for the plural "them", since English uses "land" as a whole (m2).

decisions.choice: River; north; west
decisions.reason: Readable adds "River" and the directions so that a reader can picture the area claimed.

source.text: וַיּ֥וֹסֶף ע֖וֹד יִפְתָּ֑ח וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And again added Jephthah and sent messengers to [the] king of [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: And Jephthah again sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon,
en.B: Jephthah sent messengers once more to the king of the Ammonites,
en.R: So Jephthah sent messengers again to the king of the Ammonites.

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akatuma tena wajumbe kwa mfalme wa wana wa Amoni,
sw.B: Yeftha alituma wajumbe mara nyingine kwa mfalme wa Waamoni,
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Yeftha alituma tena wajumbe kwa mfalme wa Waamoni.

es.L: Y Jefté volvió a enviar mensajeros al rey de los hijos de Amón,
es.B: Jefté envió mensajeros otra vez al rey de los amonitas,
es.R: Entonces Jefté envió otra vez mensajeros al rey de los amonitas.

decisions.choice: added again and sent: sent a second time
decisions.reason: "Add" with another verb means to do something again. Jephthah answers the king's claim with a longer message.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יִפְתָּ֑ח לֹֽא־לָקַ֤ח יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב וְאֶת־אֶ֖רֶץ בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, thus says Jephthah, not took Israel [the] land of Moab and [the] land of [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: and he said to him, "Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the sons of Ammon.
en.B: and they said to him, "This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
en.R: They said to the king, "This is Jephthah's message: Israel did not take any land from the Moabites or from the Ammonites.

sw.L: naye akamwambia, "Hivi ndivyo asemavyo Yeftha: Israeli hakuichukua nchi ya Moabu wala nchi ya wana wa Amoni.
sw.B: nao wakamwambia, "Hivi ndivyo Yeftha asemavyo: Israeli hawakuichukua nchi ya Moabu wala nchi ya Waamoni.
sw.R: Walimwambia mfalme, "Huu ndio ujumbe wa Yeftha: Israeli hawakuchukua nchi yoyote ya Wamoabu wala ya Waamoni.

es.L: y le dijo: «Así dice Jefté: Israel no tomó la tierra de Moab ni la tierra de los hijos de Amón.
es.B: y le dijeron: «Esto dice Jefté: Israel no se apoderó de la tierra de Moab ni de la tierra de los amonitas.
es.R: Le dijeron al rey: «Este es el mensaje de Jefté: Israel no les quitó tierra a los moabitas ni a los amonitas.

decisions.choice: Israel did not take the land of Moab or of Ammon: Israel kept the LORD's command
decisions.reason: The LORD told Israel not to attack Moab or Ammon or take their land, because he had given it to the descendants of Lot (Deuteronomy 2:9, 19). Jephthah's first point is that Israel obeyed.

decisions.choice: he said to him: the message spoken through the messengers
decisions.reason: The verb is singular, but the words are carried by the messengers. Jephthah's message runs from here to the end of verse 27.

decisions.choice: thus says Jephthah: the formula of a messenger
decisions.reason: A messenger began with the name of the one who sent him, then spoke in his name, using "I". Moses' message to Edom begins the same way (Numbers 20:14).

decisions.choice: they said
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "they" for the messengers, who actually speak (m2). Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: a quotation opened and left open
decisions.reason: The message runs to verse 27, so its quotation marks open here and close there. The messages Israel sent long ago (verses 17 and 19) stand inside it with single quotation marks.

source.text: כִּ֖י בַּעֲלוֹתָ֣ם מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ עַד־יַם־ס֔וּף וַיָּבֹ֖א קָדֵֽשָׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: For when they came up from Egypt, and went Israel through the wilderness to [the] Sea of Reeds, and it came to Kadesh.

en.L: For when they came up from Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness to the Sea of Reeds and came to Kadesh.
en.B: When Israel came up from Egypt, it journeyed through the wilderness as far as the Red Sea and then reached Kadesh.
en.R: When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they traveled through the desert to the Red Sea. Then they came to Kadesh.

sw.L: Kwa maana walipopanda kutoka Misri, Israeli alipita nyikani hadi Bahari ya Matete, akafika Kadeshi.
sw.B: Israeli walipopanda kutoka Misri, walisafiri kupitia nyika mpaka Bahari ya Shamu, kisha wakafika Kadeshi.
sw.R: Waisraeli walipotoka Misri, walisafiri kupitia jangwa mpaka Bahari ya Shamu. Kisha wakafika Kadeshi.

es.L: Porque cuando subieron de Egipto, Israel anduvo por el desierto hasta el mar de los Juncos y llegó a Cades.
es.B: Cuando Israel subió de Egipto, recorrió el desierto hasta el mar Rojo y luego llegó a Cades.
es.R: Cuando los israelitas salieron de Egipto, viajaron por el desierto hasta el mar Rojo. Después llegaron a Cades.

decisions.choice: through the wilderness to the Sea of Reeds and to Kadesh: the journey told in Numbers
decisions.reason: Jephthah sums up Israel's wandering after the exodus: the way to the Sea of Reeds (Numbers 14:25) and the long stay at Kadesh (Numbers 20:1; Deuteronomy 1:46).

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel crossed, and the gulfs to the south
decisions.reason: The name means "sea of reeds". It is used of the sea crossed in the exodus and of the gulfs on either side of the Sinai peninsula; here it is one stage of the wilderness journey.

decisions.choice: Red Sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name "Red Sea"; Literal keeps "Sea of Reeds", as in Numbers 21:4.

decisions.choice: "nyika" for the wilderness at Literal and Balanced, "jangwa" at Readable
decisions.reason: For this block, as in the Pentateuch drafts: the midbar is open, dry grazing land rather than sand desert, which "nyika" says; Readable uses "jangwa", the everyday word most readers know.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל מַלְאָכִ֣ים׀אֶל־מֶלֶךְ֩ אֱד֨וֹם׀לֵאמֹ֜ר אֶעְבְּרָה־נָּ֣א בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ וְלֹ֤א שָׁמַע֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֱד֔וֹם וְגַ֨ם אֶל־מֶ֧לֶךְ מוֹאָ֛ב שָׁלַ֖ח וְלֹ֣א אָבָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּקָדֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Israel messengers to [the] king of Edom, saying, let me pass please through your land, and not listened [the] king of Edom; and also to [the] king of Moab it sent, and not he was willing; and stayed Israel in Kadesh.

en.L: And Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Please let me pass through your land'; but the king of Edom did not listen. And it also sent to the king of Moab, but he was not willing. So Israel stayed at Kadesh.
en.B: Israel sent messengers to ask the king of Edom, 'Please allow us to cross your land.' But the king of Edom paid no attention. They sent the same request to the king of Moab, and he refused too. So Israel remained at Kadesh.
en.R: Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom. They asked, 'Please let us go through your country.' But the king of Edom would not listen. Israel sent the same message to the king of Moab, but he said no too. So the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.

sw.L: Naye Israeli akatuma wajumbe kwa mfalme wa Edomu, akisema, 'Tafadhali niache nipite katika nchi yako'; lakini mfalme wa Edomu hakusikiliza. Tena akatuma kwa mfalme wa Moabu, lakini hakukubali. Basi Israeli akakaa Kadeshi.
sw.B: Israeli walituma wajumbe kumwomba mfalme wa Edomu, 'Tafadhali turuhusu tupite katika nchi yako.' Lakini mfalme wa Edomu hakujali. Walimpelekea mfalme wa Moabu ombi hilo hilo, naye pia akakataa. Kwa hiyo Israeli walibaki Kadeshi.
sw.R: Israeli walituma wajumbe kwa mfalme wa Edomu. Waliomba, 'Tafadhali tuache tupite katika nchi yako.' Lakini mfalme wa Edomu hakutaka kusikiliza. Israeli walimtumia mfalme wa Moabu ujumbe ule ule, lakini naye alikataa. Kwa hiyo Waisraeli walikaa Kadeshi.

es.L: Y envió Israel mensajeros al rey de Edom, diciendo: “Déjame pasar, te ruego, por tu tierra”; pero el rey de Edom no escuchó. Y envió también al rey de Moab, pero él no quiso. Y se quedó Israel en Cades.
es.B: Israel envió mensajeros a pedirle al rey de Edom: “Por favor, déjanos atravesar tu tierra”. Pero el rey de Edom no hizo caso. Enviaron la misma petición al rey de Moab, y él también se negó. Así que Israel se quedó en Cades.
es.R: Israel envió mensajeros al rey de Edom. Le pidieron: “Por favor, déjanos pasar por tu país”. Pero el rey de Edom no quiso escuchar. Israel envió el mismo mensaje al rey de Moab, pero él también dijo que no. Así que los israelitas se quedaron en Cades.

decisions.choice: the request to the king of Edom: Numbers 20:14-21
decisions.reason: Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to ask Edom for passage, and Edom refused (Numbers 20:14-21). Jephthah's point is that Israel asked first and did not force its way.

decisions.choice: the request to the king of Moab: known only from this verse
decisions.reason: Numbers does not tell of a message to Moab, though Deuteronomy 2:29 mentions dealings with Moab on the way. Jephthah adds it to show that Israel asked both nations and was refused by both.

decisions.choice: let me pass: Israel speaks as one person
decisions.reason: The message uses "I" for the whole people, as Numbers 20:14-19 does.

decisions.choice: let us pass
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "us" for the people as a whole (m3).

decisions.choice: Israel as one speaker ("niache nipite", singular verbs) at Literal; plural verbs ("Israeli walituma", "turuhusu tupite") at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of Israel as one person (m3). Swahili can do the same with singular verbs, and Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the plural, which Swahili more naturally gives a people, as the English "let us" does.

source.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בַּמִּדְבָּ֗ר וַיָּ֜סָב אֶת־אֶ֤רֶץ אֱדוֹם֙ וְאֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב וַיָּבֹ֤א מִמִּזְרַח־שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ לְאֶ֣רֶץ מוֹאָ֔ב וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּן בְּעֵ֣בֶר אַרְנ֑וֹן וְלֹא־בָ֨אוּ֙ בִּגְב֣וּל מוֹאָ֔ב כִּ֥י אַרְנ֖וֹן גְּב֥וּל מוֹאָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And it went through the wilderness and went around [the] land of Edom and [the] land of Moab, and it came from [the] rising of [the] sun to [the] land of Moab, and they camped on [the] other side of Arnon; and not they came into [the] territory of Moab, for Arnon [was the] border of Moab.

en.L: And it went through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came to the east of the land of Moab, and they camped on the other side of the Arnon; but they did not come into the territory of Moab, for the Arnon [was] the border of Moab.
en.B: Then Israel traveled through the wilderness and went around the lands of Edom and Moab. They passed along the east side of Moab and camped on the far side of the Arnon. They did not enter Moabite territory, because the Arnon was the border of Moab.
en.R: Then the Israelites went through the desert around the countries of Edom and Moab. They went along the east side of Moab and camped on the other side of the Arnon River. They did not go into Moab at all, because the Arnon River was Moab's border.

sw.L: Naye akapita nyikani, akaizunguka nchi ya Edomu na nchi ya Moabu, akafika upande wa mashariki wa nchi ya Moabu, nao wakapiga kambi ng'ambo ya Arnoni; lakini hawakuingia katika mipaka ya Moabu, kwa maana Arnoni [ulikuwa] mpaka wa Moabu.
sw.B: Kisha Israeli walisafiri kupitia nyika, wakazizunguka nchi za Edomu na Moabu. Walipita upande wa mashariki wa Moabu, wakapiga kambi ng'ambo ya Arnoni. Hawakuingia katika eneo la Moabu, kwa sababu Arnoni ulikuwa mpaka wa Moabu.
sw.R: Kisha Waisraeli walipita jangwani wakizunguka nchi za Edomu na Moabu. Walipita upande wa mashariki wa Moabu, wakapiga kambi ng'ambo ya pili ya Mto Arnoni. Hawakuingia Moabu hata kidogo, kwa sababu Mto Arnoni ulikuwa mpaka wa Moabu.

es.L: Y anduvo por el desierto y rodeó la tierra de Edom y la tierra de Moab, y llegó por el lado donde sale el sol a la tierra de Moab, y acamparon al otro lado del Arnón; pero no entraron en el territorio de Moab, porque el Arnón [era] la frontera de Moab.
es.B: Luego Israel atravesó el desierto y rodeó las tierras de Edom y de Moab. Pasó por el lado oriental de Moab y acampó al otro lado del Arnón. No entraron en territorio moabita, porque el Arnón era la frontera de Moab.
es.R: Después los israelitas cruzaron el desierto rodeando los países de Edom y Moab. Pasaron por el lado este de Moab y acamparon al otro lado del río Arnón. No entraron en Moab en absoluto, porque el río Arnón era la frontera de Moab.

decisions.choice: around Edom and Moab, camped across the Arnon: Numbers 21:4, 10-13
decisions.reason: Israel went around Edom (Numbers 21:4) and along the edge of Moab, then camped beyond the Arnon, which Numbers 21:13 also calls the border of Moab.

decisions.choice: from the rising of the sun: on the east
decisions.reason: The place where the sun rises means the east. Israel kept to the desert side of Moab.

decisions.choice: the other side of the Arnon: north of the river
decisions.reason: The Arnon is a deep gorge flowing west into the Dead Sea. Moab lay south of it; the camp on its other side was in the land Sihon held (Numbers 21:13, 26).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־סִיח֥וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־הָאֱמֹרִ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נַעְבְּרָה־נָּ֥א בְאַרְצְךָ֖ עַד־מְקוֹמִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And sent Israel messengers to Sihon king of the Amorite[s], king of Heshbon, and said to him Israel, let us pass please through your land to my place.

en.L: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon, and Israel said to him, 'Please let us pass through your land to my place.'
en.B: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled at Heshbon, and said to him, 'Please allow us to cross your land to our own place.'
en.R: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon, the king of the Amorites, who ruled in the city of Heshbon. They said to him, 'Please let us go through your country to the land that is ours.'

sw.L: Naye Israeli akatuma wajumbe kwa Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, mfalme wa Heshboni, naye Israeli akamwambia, 'Tafadhali tuache tupite katika nchi yako mpaka mahali pangu.'
sw.B: Kisha Israeli walituma wajumbe kwa Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, aliyetawala Heshboni, wakamwambia, 'Tafadhali turuhusu tupite katika nchi yako tufike mahali petu wenyewe.'
sw.R: Kisha Israeli walituma wajumbe kwa Sihoni, mfalme wa Waamori, aliyetawala katika mji wa Heshboni. Walimwambia, 'Tafadhali tuache tupite katika nchi yako twende kwenye nchi iliyo yetu.'

es.L: Y envió Israel mensajeros a Sijón, rey de los amorreos, rey de Hesbón, y le dijo Israel: “Déjanos pasar, te ruego, por tu tierra hasta mi lugar”.
es.B: Después Israel envió mensajeros a Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que reinaba en Hesbón, y le dijo: “Por favor, déjanos atravesar tu tierra hasta nuestro lugar”.
es.R: Después Israel envió mensajeros a Sijón, el rey de los amorreos, que gobernaba en la ciudad de Hesbón. Le dijeron: “Por favor, déjanos pasar por tu país hasta la tierra que es nuestra”.

decisions.choice: the request to Sihon: Numbers 21:21-22
decisions.reason: Israel asked Sihon for passage in the same way it had asked Edom (Numbers 21:21-22). Heshbon was his royal city (Numbers 21:26).

decisions.choice: my place: the land promised to Israel, west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel asked only to pass through to the land the LORD had promised it beyond the Jordan. It did not want Sihon's land, Jephthah says; the war came from Sihon.

decisions.choice: our own place / the land that is ours
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "our" to match "us" earlier in the sentence; Literal keeps the shift from "us" to "my".

source.text: וְלֹא־הֶאֱמִ֨ין סִיח֤וֹן אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ עֲבֹ֣ר בִּגְבֻל֔וֹ וַיֶּאֱסֹ֤ף סִיחוֹן֙ אֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֔וֹ וַֽיַּחֲנ֖וּ בְּיָ֑הְצָה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם עִם־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And not trusted Sihon Israel to pass through his territory, and gathered Sihon all his people and they camped at Jahaz, and he fought with Israel.

en.L: But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory; and Sihon gathered all his people, and they camped at Jahaz, and he fought with Israel.
en.B: But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. He gathered all his forces, camped at Jahaz and attacked Israel.
en.R: But Sihon did not trust the Israelites to go peacefully through his land. So he called together his whole army. They set up camp at Jahaz, and he attacked Israel.

sw.L: Lakini Sihoni hakumwamini Israeli apite katika mipaka yake; naye Sihoni akawakusanya watu wake wote, wakapiga kambi Yahasi, akapigana na Israeli.
sw.B: Lakini Sihoni hakuwaamini Israeli wapite katika eneo lake. Aliyakusanya majeshi yake yote, akapiga kambi Yahasi, akawashambulia Israeli.
sw.R: Lakini Sihoni hakuwaamini Waisraeli kwamba wangepita kwa amani katika nchi yake. Kwa hiyo aliliita jeshi lake lote. Walipiga kambi Yahasi, naye akawashambulia Israeli.

es.L: Pero Sijón no se fió de Israel para [dejarlo] pasar por su territorio; y reunió Sijón a todo su pueblo, y acamparon en Jahaz, y peleó contra Israel.
es.B: Pero Sijón no se fió de Israel para dejarlo pasar por su territorio. Reunió a todas sus tropas, acampó en Jahaz y atacó a Israel.
es.R: Pero Sijón no confió en que los israelitas pasarían en paz por su tierra. Por eso reunió a todo su ejército. Acamparon en Jahaz, y él atacó a Israel.

decisions.choice: did not trust Israel to pass: refused out of suspicion
alternatives: did not allow Israel to pass
decisions.reason: The verb means to believe or trust. Sihon did not believe Israel would pass through peacefully. Numbers 21:23 says only that he would not allow it; Jephthah gives the reason.

decisions.choice: gathered his people at Jahaz and fought: Numbers 21:23
decisions.reason: Jephthah follows Numbers 21:23: Sihon gathered his forces, came to Jahaz and fought Israel. The war was Sihon's doing.

decisions.choice: forces / army
decisions.reason: "His people" here are the men he called out to fight; Balanced and Readable say so, as Numbers 21:23 does.

source.text: וַ֠יִּתֵּן יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל אֶת־סִיח֧וֹן וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֛וֹ בְּיַ֥ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וַיַּכּ֑וּם וַיִּירַשׁ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י יוֹשֵׁ֖ב הָאָ֥רֶץ הַהִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: And gave Yahweh God of Israel Sihon and all his people into [the] hand of Israel, and they struck them; and took possession Israel of all [the] land of the Amorite[s], who dwelt [in] that land.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them; and Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites, who lived in that land.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his forces into Israel's power, and Israel defeated them and took possession of the whole land of the Amorites who lived in that region.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, let the Israelites defeat Sihon and his whole army. So Israel took over all the land of the Amorites who lived there.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, akamtia Sihoni na watu wake wote mkononi mwa Israeli, nao wakawapiga; naye Israeli akaimiliki nchi yote ya Waamori, waliokaa katika nchi hiyo.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, aliwatia Sihoni na majeshi yake yote katika mamlaka ya Israeli, nao Israeli wakawashinda, wakaimiliki nchi yote ya Waamori waliokaa katika eneo hilo.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, aliwawezesha Waisraeli kumshinda Sihoni na jeshi lake lote. Kwa hiyo Israeli waliichukua nchi yote ya Waamori walioishi huko.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, entregó a Sijón y a todo su pueblo en mano de Israel, y los derrotaron; y tomó Israel posesión de toda la tierra de los amorreos que habitaban en aquella tierra.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, entregó a Sijón y a todas sus tropas en poder de Israel, e Israel los derrotó y tomó posesión de toda la tierra de los amorreos que vivían en aquella región.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, hizo que los israelitas derrotaran a Sijón y a todo su ejército. Así Israel se quedó con toda la tierra de los amorreos que vivían allí.

decisions.choice: the LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon into Israel's hand: the victory was the LORD's
decisions.reason: Jephthah's argument rests on this: Israel did not take the land by its own choice, the LORD gave it (Numbers 21:34; Deuteronomy 2:31-33). The full title "the God of Israel" sets the LORD against the god of the Ammonite king (verse 24).

decisions.choice: took possession of: took over as its own
decisions.reason: The verb means to take land and hold it as an inheritance. It returns in verses 22-24, where it also means to drive out the people who held it.

decisions.choice: into Israel's power
decisions.reason: Balanced says "power" for the picture of "hand", as Judges does with this phrase; Literal keeps "hand", and Readable says what it meant.

source.text: וַיִּ֣ירְשׁ֔וּ אֵ֖ת כָּל־גְּב֣וּל הָאֱמֹרִ֑י מֵֽאַרְנוֹן֙ וְעַד־הַיַּבֹּ֔ק וּמִן־הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר וְעַד־הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took possession of all [the] territory of the Amorite[s], from Arnon and to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness and to the Jordan.

en.L: And they took possession of all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness to the Jordan.
en.B: They took over the whole Amorite territory, from the Arnon in the south to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness across to the Jordan.
en.R: They took over all the land of the Amorites. It reached from the Arnon River north to the Jabbok River, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.

sw.L: Nao wakaimiliki mipaka yote ya Waamori, kutoka Arnoni hadi Yaboki, na kutoka nyika hadi Yordani.
sw.B: Waliimiliki nchi yote ya Waamori, kutoka Arnoni upande wa kusini hadi Yaboki, na kutoka nyika hadi Yordani.
sw.R: Waliichukua nchi yote ya Waamori. Ilienea kutoka Mto Arnoni kaskazini hadi Mto Yaboki, na kutoka jangwa upande wa mashariki hadi Mto Yordani upande wa magharibi.

es.L: Y tomaron posesión de todo el territorio de los amorreos, desde el Arnón hasta el Jaboc, y desde el desierto hasta el Jordán.
es.B: Se apoderaron de todo el territorio amorreo, desde el Arnón, en el sur, hasta el Jaboc, y desde el desierto hasta el Jordán.
es.R: Se quedaron con toda la tierra de los amorreos. Iba desde el río Arnón, al norte hasta el río Jaboc, y desde el desierto, al este, hasta el río Jordán, al oeste.

decisions.choice: from the Arnon to the Jabbok, from the wilderness to the Jordan: the land of Sihon
decisions.reason: The same bounds as the king's claim (verse 13), with the east-west line added: the desert on the east, the Jordan on the west. Numbers 21:24 gives the north-south bounds. Jephthah's point is that this was Amorite land, not Ammonite.

decisions.choice: River; north; east; west
decisions.reason: Readable adds "River" and directions so that a reader can picture the area.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֞ה יְהוָ֣ה׀אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הוֹרִישׁ֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י מִפְּנֵ֖י עַמּ֣וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּירָשֶֽׁנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now Yahweh God of Israel has dispossessed the Amorite[s] from before his people Israel, and you will take possession of it?

en.L: And now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites from before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel, and you would take possession of it?
en.B: So now that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel, are you to take their land?
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, forced the Amorites out of their land to make room for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people Israel. So do you think you can take that land now?

sw.L: Na sasa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, amewafukuza Waamori mbele ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Israeli, nawe utaimiliki?
sw.B: Basi sasa kwa kuwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, amewafukuza Waamori mbele ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Israeli, je, wewe utaichukua nchi yao?
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mungu wa Israeli, aliwafukuza Waamori kutoka katika nchi yao ili kuwapa nafasi watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} Israeli. Basi unadhani unaweza kuichukua nchi hiyo sasa?

es.L: Y ahora {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, ha desposeído a los amorreos de delante de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo Israel, ¿y tú [la] poseerías?
es.B: Ahora que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, ha expulsado a los amorreos delante de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo Israel, ¿vas tú a quedarte con su tierra?
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Dios de Israel, echó a los amorreos de su tierra para hacerle lugar a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo Israel. ¿Y crees que ahora tú puedes quedarte con esa tierra?

decisions.choice: has dispossessed: drove out the people who held the land
decisions.reason: The verb is the causative of "take possession" (verse 21): the LORD made the Amorites lose the land so that Israel could hold it. The same word ends this verse, so the question sets the LORD's act against the king's wish.

decisions.choice: and you will take possession of it?: a question that expects "no"
decisions.reason: There is no question word, but the stress on "you" makes it a scornful question: are you going to take what the LORD gave Israel?

decisions.choice: to make room for
decisions.reason: Readable says what "from before his people" means: the Amorites were driven out so that Israel could live there.

source.text: הֲלֹ֞א אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר יוֹרִֽישְׁךָ֛ כְּמ֥וֹשׁ אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ אוֹת֥וֹ תִירָ֑שׁ וְאֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹרִ֜ישׁ יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵ֛ינוּ מִפָּנֵ֖ינוּ אוֹת֥וֹ נִירָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] not that which causes you to possess Chemosh your god, it you will possess? And all that has dispossessed Yahweh our God from before us, it we will possess.

en.L: Is it not [so that] whatever Chemosh your god gives you to possess, that you will possess? And all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has dispossessed from before us, that we will possess.
en.B: Do you not take possession of whatever your god Chemosh gives you? In the same way, we will possess all the land of those whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has driven out before us.
en.R: You keep whatever land your god Chemosh gives you, do you not? In the same way, we will keep all the land of the people that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God has driven out for us.

sw.L: Je, si kwamba kile anachokupa Kemoshi mungu wako ukimiliki, ndicho utakachokimiliki? Na kila kitu ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu amekiondoa mbele yetu, hicho ndicho tutakachokimiliki.
sw.B: Je, wewe hukimiliki chochote ambacho mungu wako Kemoshi anakupa? Vivyo hivyo sisi tutaimiliki nchi yote ya wale ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu amewafukuza mbele yetu.
sw.R: Wewe unaitunza nchi yoyote ambayo mungu wako Kemoshi anakupa, sivyo? Vivyo hivyo, sisi tutaitunza nchi yote ya watu ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu amewafukuza kwa ajili yetu.

es.L: ¿No [es así], que lo que Quemos tu dios te da a poseer, eso posees? Y todo lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios ha desposeído de delante de nosotros, eso poseeremos.
es.B: ¿No tomas tú posesión de todo lo que te da tu dios Quemos? De la misma manera, nosotros poseeremos toda la tierra de aquellos a quienes {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios ha expulsado delante de nosotros.
es.R: Tú te quedas con la tierra que te da tu dios Quemos, ¿no es cierto? De la misma manera, nosotros nos quedaremos con toda la tierra de los pueblos que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios ha echado para darnos lugar.

decisions.choice: Chemosh your god: the god of Moab
alternatives: Chemosh as a god worshiped in Ammon too
decisions.reason: Chemosh was the national god of Moab (Numbers 21:29; 1 Kings 11:7, 33); the god of Ammon was Milcom (1 Kings 11:5). Jephthah may name Chemosh because the land in dispute had once been Moab's (Numbers 21:26), or because the Ammonite king ruled Moabite land as well. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: what Chemosh gives you: an argument on the king's own terms
decisions.reason: Jephthah reasons from what the king himself believes: you keep what you think your god gave you, so we keep what the LORD gave us. He does not grant that Chemosh is a true god; in verse 27 the LORD alone is the judge between the two peoples.

decisions.choice: is it not ...?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The first half is a question the king must agree with; the second half draws the conclusion for Israel.

decisions.choice: all the land of those whom / of the people that
decisions.reason: "Dispossess" has people as its object; Balanced and Readable add "land" so that it is clear what Israel will possess.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה הֲט֥וֹב טוֹב֙ אַתָּ֔ה מִבָּלָ֥ק בֶּן־צִפּ֖וֹר מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֑ב הֲר֥וֹב רָב֙ עִם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִם־נִלְחֹ֥ם נִלְחַ֖ם בָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And now [are] really better you than Balak son of Zippor king of Moab? Did he really quarrel with Israel, or did he really fight against them?

en.L: And now, are you really better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever quarrel with Israel, or did he ever fight against them?
en.B: Are you really a better man than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever dispute with Israel or make war on them?
en.R: Do you think you are better than Balak son of Zippor, who was king of Moab? He never argued with Israel about the land, and he never went to war against them.

sw.L: Na sasa, je, wewe u bora kweli kuliko Balaki mwana wa Zipori, mfalme wa Moabu? Je, aliwahi kweli kugombana na Israeli, au aliwahi kweli kupigana nao?
sw.B: Je, wewe kweli ni mtu bora kuliko Balaki mwana wa Zipori, mfalme wa Moabu? Je, aliwahi kubishana na Israeli au kupigana vita nao?
sw.R: Unadhani wewe ni bora kuliko Balaki mwana wa Zipori, aliyekuwa mfalme wa Moabu? Yeye hakuwahi kubishana na Israeli juu ya nchi, wala hakuwahi kwenda vitani dhidi yao.

es.L: Y ahora, ¿eres tú acaso mejor que Balac hijo de Zipor, rey de Moab? ¿Acaso disputó él con Israel, o acaso peleó contra ellos?
es.B: ¿Eres tú realmente mejor que Balac hijo de Zipor, rey de Moab? ¿Alguna vez disputó él con Israel o le hizo la guerra?
es.R: ¿Crees que eres mejor que Balac hijo de Zipor, que fue rey de Moab? Él nunca discutió con Israel por la tierra, y nunca les hizo la guerra.

decisions.choice: Balak son of Zippor: the king of Moab who feared Israel
decisions.reason: Balak saw what Israel had done to the Amorites and hired Balaam to curse them (Numbers 22-24), but he never took the land back by war. Joshua 24:9 speaks of his hostility through Balaam; Jephthah's point is that he did not claim Sihon's land.

decisions.choice: really better ... did he really quarrel ... did he really fight: questions made stronger
decisions.reason: Each verb is doubled for stress. The questions all expect the answer "no".

decisions.choice: statements for the last two questions
decisions.reason: Readable gives the answer the questions expect, so the reader does not miss the point. It adds "about the land", the matter in dispute.

records.literal_gloss: When dwelt Israel in Heshbon and in its daughters, and in Aroer and in its daughters, and in all the cities that [are] on [the] sides of Arnon, three hundred years, and why not did you recover [them] in that time?

en.L: When Israel lived in Heshbon and in its daughters, and in Aroer and in its daughters, and in all the cities that [are] beside the Arnon, 300 years, why did you not recover [them] at that time?
en.B: Israel has lived in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the towns along the Arnon for 300 years. Why did you not take them back during all that time?
en.R: Israel has lived for 300 years in Heshbon and Aroer and the villages around them, and in all the towns along the Arnon River. Why did you not take them back during all that time?

sw.L: Israeli alipokaa Heshboni na binti zake, na Aroeri na binti zake, na katika miji yote iliyo kando ya Arnoni, miaka 300, kwa nini hamkuirudisha wakati huo?
sw.B: Israeli wamekaa Heshboni na vijiji vyake, Aroeri na vijiji vyake, na katika miji yote iliyo kando ya Arnoni kwa miaka 300. Kwa nini hamkuirudisha katika muda wote huo?
sw.R: Israeli wamekaa kwa miaka 300 katika Heshboni na Aroeri na vijiji vinavyoizunguka, na katika miji yote iliyo kando ya Mto Arnoni. Kwa nini hamkuirudisha katika muda wote huo?

es.L: Mientras Israel habitó en Hesbón y en sus hijas, y en Aroer y en sus hijas, y en todas las ciudades que [están] junto al Arnón, 300 años, ¿por qué no [las] recobraron en aquel tiempo?
es.B: Israel ha vivido 300 años en Hesbón y sus aldeas, en Aroer y sus aldeas y en todas las ciudades a orillas del Arnón. ¿Por qué no las recuperaron en todo ese tiempo?
es.R: Israel ha vivido 300 años en Hesbón y en Aroer y en las aldeas que las rodean, y en todas las ciudades junto al río Arnón. ¿Por qué no las recuperaron en todo ese tiempo?

decisions.choice: its daughters: the villages that belonged to a town
decisions.reason: "Daughters" of a town are the smaller places around it that depended on it (Numbers 21:25).

decisions.choice: Heshbon, Aroer, the towns beside the Arnon: the land Israel settled
decisions.reason: Heshbon had been Sihon's royal city (Numbers 21:26). Aroer stood on the edge of the Arnon gorge (Deuteronomy 2:36). The "sides" (literally "hands") of the Arnon are its banks.

decisions.choice: 300 years: a round number for a very long time
decisions.reason: The years given in Judges 3-10 for times of oppression and peace add up to more than this, so the number fits as a round figure. Jephthah's point is that the claim comes far too late.

decisions.choice: villages
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "villages" for "daughters" (m1), as Numbers 21:25 does.

source.text: וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ לֹֽא־חָטָ֣אתִי לָ֔ךְ וְאַתָּ֞ה עֹשֶׂ֥ה אִתִּ֛י רָעָ֖ה לְהִלָּ֣חֶם בִּ֑י יִשְׁפֹּ֨ט יְהוָ֤ה הַשֹּׁפֵט֙ הַיּ֔וֹם בֵּ֚ין בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּבֵ֖ין בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And I not have sinned against you, and you [are] doing with me evil by fighting against me; may judge Yahweh the Judge today between [the] sons of Israel and between [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: And I have not sinned against you, but you are doing me wrong by fighting against me. May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Judge, judge today between the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and the sons of Ammon."
en.B: I have not wronged you, but you are wronging me by making war on me. Let {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who is the Judge, settle the case today between the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and the Ammonites."
en.R: I have done nothing wrong to you. But you are doing wrong to me by attacking me. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is the judge. Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} decide today who is right, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} or the Ammonites."

sw.L: Mimi sikukutenda dhambi, lakini wewe unanitendea uovu kwa kupigana nami. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, Mwamuzi, na aamue leo kati ya wana wa Israeli na wana wa Amoni."
sw.B: Mimi sijakukosea, lakini wewe unanikosea kwa kunishambulia kwa vita. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliye Mwamuzi, na aamue shauri hili leo kati ya Waisraeli na Waamoni."
sw.R: Sijakufanyia kosa lolote. Lakini wewe unanikosea kwa kunishambulia. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ndiye mwamuzi. Basi {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aamue leo ni nani aliye sawa, Waisraeli au Waamoni."

es.L: Y yo no he pecado contra ti, pero tú me haces mal al pelear contra mí. Juzgue hoy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, el Juez, entre los hijos de Israel y los hijos de Amón».
es.B: Yo no te he hecho ningún mal, pero tú me haces mal al hacerme la guerra. Que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que es el Juez, decida hoy el pleito entre los israelitas y los amonitas».
es.R: Yo no te he hecho nada malo. Pero tú me haces mal al atacarme. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} es el juez. Que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} decida hoy quién tiene razón, los israelitas o los amonitas».

decisions.choice: sinned against you ... doing evil with me: wronged in a matter of right
decisions.reason: "Sin against" here means to wrong another party, as in a dispute between peoples (1 Samuel 24:12). Jephthah says the wrong is all on Ammon's side.

decisions.choice: the LORD, the Judge, judge: God settles the dispute
decisions.reason: This is the only place in Judges where the title "the judge" is given in the singular, and it is given to the LORD. The human judges lead and rescue; the LORD is the one who decides between the nations, as Abraham calls him "the Judge of all the earth" (Genesis 18:25). The battle will show his verdict.

decisions.choice: settle the case / decide
decisions.reason: "Judge" here means to decide a case, not to lead Israel, so Balanced says "settle the case" and Readable "decide"; the title "the Judge" stays.

decisions.choice: who is right
decisions.reason: Readable says what the LORD is asked to decide.

decisions.choice: "Mwamuzi" (the Judge) for the LORD, the same word as "mwamuzi", the title of the book's judges
decisions.reason: "Mwamuzi" is the one who decides a dispute between two sides, which is what Jephthah asks of the LORD here, and it is the word this translation uses for the judges of Israel, so the link the Hebrew makes is kept. "Hakimu" is a court magistrate.

records.literal_gloss: And not listened [the] king of [the] sons of Ammon to [the] words of Jephthah that he sent to him.

en.L: But the king of the sons of Ammon did not listen to the words of Jephthah that he sent to him.
en.B: But the king of the Ammonites paid no attention to the message Jephthah sent him.
en.R: But the king of the Ammonites would not listen to Jephthah's message.

sw.L: Lakini mfalme wa wana wa Amoni hakuyasikiliza maneno ya Yeftha aliyomtumia.
sw.B: Lakini mfalme wa Waamoni hakuujali ujumbe ambao Yeftha alimtumia.
sw.R: Lakini mfalme wa Waamoni hakutaka kusikiliza ujumbe wa Yeftha.

es.L: Pero el rey de los hijos de Amón no escuchó las palabras que Jefté le envió.
es.B: Pero el rey de los amonitas no hizo caso del mensaje que Jefté le envió.
es.R: Pero el rey de los amonitas no quiso escuchar el mensaje de Jefté.

decisions.choice: did not listen: refused to accept the message
decisions.reason: "Listen" here means to heed. The king rejects Jephthah's case, and the matter goes to battle, where the LORD will judge (verse 27).

source.text: וַתְּהִ֤י עַל־יִפְתָּח֙ ר֣וּחַ יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּעֲבֹ֥ר אֶת־הַגִּלְעָ֖ד וְאֶת־מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲבֹר֙ אֶת־מִצְפֵּ֣ה גִלְעָ֔ד וּמִמִּצְפֵּ֣ה גִלְעָ֔ד עָבַ֖ר בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And was on Jephthah [the] Spirit of Yahweh, and he passed through the Gilead and Manasseh, and he passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he passed on [to the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: And the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, and passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he passed on [to] the sons of Ammon.
en.B: Then the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Jephthah. He went through Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he went on against the Ammonites.
en.R: Then the Spirit of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came on Jephthah. He went through Gilead and Manasseh to gather an army. He passed through Mizpah in Gilead, and from there he went on to fight the Ammonites.

sw.L: Naye Roho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamjia Yeftha, naye akapita katika Gileadi na Manase, akapita Mizpa ya Gileadi, na kutoka Mizpa ya Gileadi akaendelea [kwa] wana wa Amoni.
sw.B: Kisha Roho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimjia Yeftha. Alipita katika Gileadi na Manase, akapita Mizpa ya Gileadi, na kutoka Mizpa ya Gileadi akaendelea kuwashambulia Waamoni.
sw.R: Kisha Roho wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimjia Yeftha. Alipita katika Gileadi na Manase ili kukusanya jeshi. Alipita Mizpa ya Gileadi, na kutoka huko akaendelea kwenda kupigana na Waamoni.

es.L: Y vino sobre Jefté el Espíritu {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y pasó por Galaad y Manasés, y pasó por Mizpa de Galaad, y de Mizpa de Galaad pasó [hacia] los hijos de Amón.
es.B: Entonces el Espíritu {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino sobre Jefté. Recorrió Galaad y Manasés, pasó por Mizpa de Galaad, y desde Mizpa de Galaad avanzó contra los amonitas.
es.R: Entonces el Espíritu {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} vino sobre Jefté. Él recorrió Galaad y Manasés para reunir un ejército. Pasó por Mizpa, en Galaad, y desde allí siguió adelante para pelear contra los amonitas.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of the LORD came on Jephthah: the LORD equips him to lead
decisions.reason: As with Othniel (3:10) and Gideon (6:34), the Spirit gives the leader power to lead Israel to victory. The Spirit comes on Jephthah before he makes his vow (verses 30-31); the story does not say the LORD asked for a vow.

decisions.choice: passed through Gilead and Manasseh: gathering men for war
decisions.reason: Jephthah went through the lands of the eastern tribes, most likely calling out fighters, as Gideon did (6:35). Manasseh here is the half of the tribe settled east of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: passed on to the sons of Ammon: advanced against them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no word for "to"; the verb with the people as its object means he moved on against them.

decisions.choice: to gather an army
decisions.reason: Readable states the likely purpose of the journey (m2); the Hebrew does not say it outright.

decisions.choice: "Roho wa BWANA alimjia" (the Spirit of the LORD came to him) at every level, with "Roho" capitalised
decisions.reason: As agreed for Judges in every language: "kumjia" says that the Spirit came upon the man for a task, which is the sense here (m1); the Literal "was on" would read in Swahili as a lasting state.

decisions.choice: "el Espíritu del SEÑOR vino sobre"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for every Spanish block of Judges: "vino sobre" keeps the Hebrew picture of the Spirit coming upon a person to equip him to lead (m1), and "Espíritu" keeps its capital.

decisions.choice: if you indeed give them into my hand: a vow made before battle
decisions.reason: Israel made a vow in nearly the same words before fighting the king of Arad (Numbers 21:2). A vow was a promise to give God something if he granted a request (Genesis 28:20-22; 1 Samuel 1:11), and once made it had to be kept (Numbers 30:3; Deuteronomy 23:22-24).

decisions.choice: indeed give: the verb doubled for stress
decisions.reason: The repeated verb makes the condition strong: if you will surely give. It shows how much Jephthah wants the victory assured.

decisions.choice: the vow runs into verse 31
decisions.reason: The vow is one sentence across verses 30-31, so its quotation opens here and closes at the end of verse 31.

en.R: then when I come home safe from the battle, whoever or whatever comes out of my house first to meet me will belong to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will offer it up as a burnt offering."
