sw.B: basi yeyote au chochote kitakachotoka katika milango ya nyumba yangu kunilaki ninaporudi salama kutoka kwa Waamoni kitakuwa cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nami nitakitoa kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa."
sw.R: basi nitakaporudi nyumbani salama kutoka vitani, yeyote au chochote kitakachotoka kwanza nyumbani mwangu kunilaki kitakuwa mali ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitakitoa kuwa sadaka ya kuteketezwa."

es.L: el que salga, el que salga de las puertas de mi casa a mi encuentro cuando yo vuelva en paz de los hijos de Amón, será {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y lo ofreceré [en] holocausto».
es.B: entonces lo que salga por las puertas de mi casa a recibirme cuando yo vuelva sano y salvo de pelear con los amonitas, sea quien sea, será {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y lo ofreceré en holocausto».
es.R: entonces, cuando yo vuelva a casa sano y salvo de la batalla, lo primero que salga de mi casa a recibirme, sea persona o animal, será {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Lo ofreceré como holocausto, una ofrenda quemada por completo».

decisions.choice: the one coming out: whoever or whatever comes out, left open
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "the one coming out", a masculine form that Hebrew uses both for a person and for an animal or thing; it has no separate neuter. Some take Jephthah to mean a person: "to come out of the doors of my house to meet me" is what people do, and women came out to welcome a victor with song and dance (Exodus 15:20; 1 Samuel 18:6), as his daughter does in verse 34. Others take him to mean an animal: Israelite houses often sheltered animals on the ground floor, and a burnt offering was an animal (Leviticus 1). The words do not settle which he had in mind, so they are kept open.

decisions.choice: it will be the LORD's, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering: two parts of one promise
alternatives: it will be the LORD's, or I will offer it up as a burnt offering
decisions.reason: The plain sense is that what comes out will be given to the LORD by being offered as a burnt offering. Some read the second "and" as "or": it will belong to the LORD, or, if it is fit for sacrifice, be offered. That reading bears on verse 39, but "and" is the usual sense of the word.

decisions.choice: a burnt offering: an offering wholly burned on the altar
decisions.reason: A burnt offering was killed and burned whole for the LORD (Leviticus 1:9). The law strictly forbids offering people as sacrifices (Leviticus 18:21; 20:2-5; Deuteronomy 12:31; 18:10), and the LORD had not asked for this vow.

decisions.choice: when I return in peace: when I come back safe and victorious
decisions.reason: "In peace" means unharmed. For a war leader, coming home safe means coming home the winner.

decisions.choice: whoever or whatever comes out
decisions.reason: English has to choose between "whoever" and "whatever". Balanced and Readable name both so that they keep the question open as the Hebrew does (m1). Literal keeps "the [one] coming out".

decisions.choice: first
decisions.reason: Readable adds "first": the vow is about the one who comes out to meet him on his return, which means the first to reach him.

decisions.choice: the ki- class ("kile kitakachotoka", "nitakitoa") for the one who comes out; Balanced and Readable add "yeyote au chochote" (whoever or whatever)
decisions.reason: Swahili must give the one who comes out a noun class, and the person class would decide what the Hebrew leaves open (m1). The ki- class can stand for an unnamed thing or being; Balanced and Readable spell out both, as the English does, and the verbs keep the ki- agreement.

decisions.choice: "lo que salga ..., sea quien sea" (B); "sea persona o animal" (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "lo que" can point to a person or a thing, which keeps the Hebrew open as the meaning decision reads it (m1); Balanced adds "sea quien sea" and Readable "sea persona o animal" so the reader does not hear only an animal, as the English "whoever or whatever" does.

source.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֥ר יִפְתָּ֛ח אֶל־בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן לְהִלָּ֣חֶם בָּ֑ם וַיִתְּנֵ֥םיְהוָ֖ה בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And passed on Jephthah to [the] sons of Ammon to fight against them, and gave them Yahweh into his hand.

en.L: And Jephthah passed on to the sons of Ammon to fight against them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave them into his hand.
en.B: So Jephthah crossed over to the Ammonites to fight them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed them over to him.
en.R: Then Jephthah went to fight the Ammonites, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave him victory over them.

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akaendelea kwa wana wa Amoni kupigana nao, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia mkononi mwake.
sw.B: Basi Yeftha alivuka kwenda kwa Waamoni kupigana nao, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia mikononi mwake.
sw.R: Kisha Yeftha alikwenda kupigana na Waamoni, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akampa ushindi juu yao.

es.L: Y pasó Jefté [hacia] los hijos de Amón para pelear contra ellos, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} los entregó en su mano.
es.B: Así que Jefté marchó contra los amonitas para pelear con ellos, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se los entregó.
es.R: Entonces Jefté fue a pelear contra los amonitas, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio la victoria sobre ellos.

decisions.choice: the LORD gave them into his hand: the LORD grants the victory
decisions.reason: The words answer verse 9 and the vow's own condition (verse 30) in the same terms. The narrator says the LORD gave the victory; he does not say the vow won it.

decisions.choice: gave him victory over them
decisions.reason: Readable says what "gave them into his hand" means.

source.text: וַיַּכֵּ֡ם מֵעֲרוֹעֵר֩ וְעַד־בּוֹאֲךָ֨מִנִּ֜ית עֶשְׂרִ֣ים עִ֗יר וְעַד֙ אָבֵ֣ל כְּרָמִ֔ים מַכָּ֖ה גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וַיִּכָּֽנְעוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֔וֹן מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he struck them from Aroer and until your coming [to] Minnith, twenty cities, and to Abel-keramim, a blow great very; and were humbled [the] sons of Ammon before [the] sons of Israel.

en.L: And he struck them from Aroer until you come to Minnith, twenty cities, and as far as Abel-keramim, a very great blow. And the sons of Ammon were humbled before the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel.
en.B: He defeated them with a great slaughter from Aroer to the area of Minnith, twenty towns, and as far as Abel-keramim. So the Ammonites were brought under the power of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.
en.R: He completely defeated them. He attacked twenty of their towns, from Aroer to near Minnith, and as far as Abel-keramim. So the Ammonites were brought under the control of the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

sw.L: Naye akawapiga kutoka Aroeri mpaka unapofika Minithi, miji ishirini, na hadi Abel-keramimu, pigo kubwa sana. Na wana wa Amoni wakanyenyekezwa mbele ya wana wa Israeli.
sw.B: Aliwashinda kwa mauaji makubwa kutoka Aroeri hadi eneo la Minithi, miji ishirini, na mpaka Abel-keramimu. Hivyo Waamoni wakawekwa chini ya mamlaka ya Waisraeli.
sw.R: Aliwashinda kabisa. Aliishambulia miji yao ishirini, kutoka Aroeri mpaka karibu na Minithi, na hadi Abel-keramimu. Kwa hiyo Waamoni wakawa chini ya utawala wa Waisraeli.

es.L: Y los hirió desde Aroer hasta llegar a Minit, veinte ciudades, y hasta Abel-keramim, con una derrota muy grande. Y fueron humillados los hijos de Amón delante de los hijos de Israel.
es.B: Los derrotó con gran matanza desde Aroer hasta las cercanías de Minit, veinte ciudades, y hasta Abel-keramim. Así los amonitas quedaron sometidos al poder de los israelitas.
es.R: Los derrotó por completo. Atacó veinte de sus ciudades, desde Aroer hasta cerca de Minit, y hasta Abel-keramim. Así los amonitas quedaron bajo el dominio de los israelitas.

decisions.choice: Aroer, Minnith, Abel-keramim: towns toward the heart of Ammon
decisions.reason: Minnith and Abel-keramim ("meadow of vineyards") cannot now be located with certainty; they lay in or near Ammonite land. This Aroer may be the one "facing Rabbah", the Ammonite capital (Joshua 13:25), rather than the Aroer on the Arnon (verse 26).

decisions.choice: until your coming to Minnith: up to the approach to Minnith
decisions.reason: "Until you come to" is a way of marking the end of a route, as a traveler would describe it.

decisions.choice: the sons of Ammon were humbled: brought low, as earlier enemies were
decisions.reason: The same phrase ends the stories of Ehud (3:30), Deborah (4:23) and Gideon (8:28). The oppression begun in 10:7-9 is ended.

decisions.choice: were brought under the power / control of
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what being "humbled before" another people meant: losing power to them.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יִפְתָּ֣ח הַמִּצְפָּה֮ אֶל־בֵּיתוֹ֒ וְהִנֵּ֤ה בִתּוֹ֙ יֹצֵ֣את לִקְרָאת֔וֹ בְתֻפִּ֖ים וּבִמְחֹל֑וֹת וְרַק֙ הִ֣יא יְחִידָ֔ה אֵֽין־ל֥וֹ מִמֶּ֛נּוּ בֵּ֖ן אוֹ־בַֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Jephthah [to] Mizpah to his house, and look, his daughter coming out to meet him with tambourines and with dances; and only she [was] an only [child]; not was to him from him son or daughter.

en.L: And Jephthah came to Mizpah, to his house, and look, his daughter [was] coming out to meet him with tambourines and with dancing; and she [was] his one and only [child]; besides her he had neither son nor daughter.
en.B: When Jephthah reached his home in Mizpah, out came his daughter to meet him, dancing to the beat of tambourines. She was his one and only child; apart from her he had no son or daughter.
en.R: When Jephthah came back to his home in Mizpah, his daughter came out to meet him. She was playing a tambourine and dancing. She was his only child. He had no other sons or daughters.

sw.L: Naye Yeftha akafika Mizpa, nyumbani kwake, na tazama, binti yake [alikuwa] akitoka kumlaki kwa matari na kwa kucheza; naye [alikuwa] mtoto wake mmoja tu; zaidi yake hakuwa na mwana wala binti.
sw.B: Yeftha alipofika nyumbani kwake Mizpa, binti yake alitoka kumlaki, akicheza kwa mdundo wa matari. Yeye alikuwa mtoto wake wa pekee; mbali naye hakuwa na mwana wala binti.
sw.R: Yeftha aliporudi nyumbani kwake Mizpa, binti yake alitoka kumlaki. Alikuwa akipiga matari na kucheza. Alikuwa mtoto wake wa pekee. Hakuwa na wana wala binti wengine.

es.L: Y llegó Jefté a Mizpa, a su casa, y he aquí que su hija salía a su encuentro con panderos y con danzas; y ella [era] su única [hija]; fuera de ella no tenía hijo ni hija.
es.B: Cuando Jefté llegó a su casa en Mizpa, su hija salió a recibirlo bailando al son de los panderos. Era su única hija; aparte de ella no tenía ningún otro hijo ni hija.
es.R: Cuando Jefté volvió a su casa en Mizpa, su hija salió a recibirlo. Tocaba el pandero y bailaba. Era su única hija. No tenía otros hijos ni hijas.

decisions.choice: coming out to meet him with tambourines and dancing: the welcome for a victor
decisions.reason: Women went out with drums and dancing to celebrate a victory (Exodus 15:20; 1 Samuel 18:6). The words "coming out to meet him" repeat the vow (verse 31): the reader sees at once who has come out.

decisions.choice: an only child: the same word as Isaac, Abraham's only son
decisions.reason: The word is used of Isaac when God tells Abraham to offer him (Genesis 22:2, 12, 16). There God stops the sacrifice and provides a ram; here no voice from heaven speaks. With an only child, Jephthah's family line also ends.

decisions.choice: not was to him from him son or daughter: he had no child besides her
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "from him", which may mean "of his own": he had no other child of his own. A small change in one letter would give "besides her". Either way the sense is that she was his only child.

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word draws attention to a sudden sight. Literal says "look"; Balanced shows the surprise with "out came"; Readable simply tells what happened.

source.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִרְאוֹת֨וֹ אוֹתָ֜הּ וַיִּקְרַ֣ע אֶת־בְּגָדָ֗יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֲהָ֤הּ בִּתִּי֙ הַכְרֵ֣עַ הִכְרַעְתִּ֔נִי וְאַ֖תְּ הָיִ֣יתְבְּעֹֽכְרָ֑י וְאָנֹכִ֗י פָּצִ֤יתִי־פִי֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א אוּכַ֖ל לָשֽׁוּב׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was when he saw her, and he tore his clothes and said, ah, my daughter! Indeed you have brought me low, and you, you have become among those troubling me; and I, I have opened my mouth to Yahweh, and not I am able to turn back.

en.L: And it was, when he saw her, that he tore his clothes and said, "Ah, my daughter! You have brought me down utterly, and you have become one of those who trouble me. I have opened my mouth to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I cannot turn back."
en.B: As soon as he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried, "Oh, my daughter! You have struck me down! You have become the one who brings ruin on me. I have given my word to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I cannot go back on it."
en.R: When Jephthah saw her, he tore his clothes in grief. He cried out, "Oh no, my daughter! You have broken my heart! You have brought terrible trouble on me! I made a promise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I cannot take it back."

sw.L: Ikawa alipomwona, akararua mavazi yake, akasema, "Ole, binti yangu! Hakika umenishusha chini kabisa, nawe umekuwa mmoja wa wale wanaonitaabisha. Mimi nimefungua kinywa changu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nami siwezi kurudi nyuma."
sw.B: Mara alipomwona, alirarua mavazi yake, akalia, "Ole wangu, binti yangu! Umeniangusha kabisa! Umekuwa wewe unayeniletea maafa. Nimetoa ahadi kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, nami siwezi kuirudisha nyuma."
sw.R: Yeftha alipomwona, aliyararua mavazi yake kwa huzuni. Alilia, "Ole wangu, binti yangu! Umenivunja moyo! Umeniletea taabu kubwa! Nilimwahidi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} jambo, nami siwezi kulirudisha."

es.L: Y sucedió que cuando la vio, rasgó sus vestidos y dijo: «¡Ay, hija mía! Me has abatido por completo, y tú has venido a ser de los que me traen desgracia. Yo he abierto mi boca {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y no puedo volverme atrás».
es.B: En cuanto la vio, se rasgó la ropa y exclamó: «¡Ay, hija mía! ¡Me has destrozado! Tú eres la que me trae la ruina. He dado mi palabra {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y no puedo retractarme».
es.R: Cuando Jefté la vio, se rasgó la ropa de dolor. Gritó: «¡Ay, no, hija mía! ¡Me has partido el corazón! ¡Me has traído una desgracia terrible! Le hice una promesa {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, y no puedo echarme atrás».

decisions.choice: he tore his clothes: a sign of deep grief
decisions.reason: Tearing one's clothes showed sorrow or horror (Genesis 37:34; Joshua 7:6).

decisions.choice: those troubling me: the word used of Achan
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring disaster on someone. It is used of Achan, who brought disaster on Israel and was punished in the valley of Achor, "trouble" (Joshua 7:25-26). Jephthah speaks as though his daughter had brought this on him, though the vow was his.

decisions.choice: I have opened my mouth to the LORD: I have made a vow
decisions.reason: To open the mouth to the LORD is to make a vow to him (Psalm 66:14). A vow was to be kept: "he must do all that goes out of his mouth" (Numbers 30:3).

decisions.choice: I cannot turn back: Jephthah believes the vow cannot be undone
decisions.reason: The law let a person vowed to the LORD be redeemed by paying a set price (Leviticus 27:1-8), and a rash oath could be confessed and atoned for (Leviticus 5:4-6). The story does not say whether Jephthah knew of these or sought them.

decisions.choice: struck me down / broken my heart
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the strong doubled verb ("you have utterly brought me low") into plain words of grief.

source.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו אָבִי֙ פָּצִ֤יתָה אֶת־פִּ֨יךָ֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה עֲשֵׂ֣ה לִ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר יָצָ֣א מִפִּ֑יךָ אַחֲרֵ֡י אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂה֩ לְךָ֙ יְהוָ֧ה נְקָמ֛וֹת מֵאֹיְבֶ֖יךָ מִבְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to him, my father, you have opened your mouth to Yahweh; do to me according to what has gone out from your mouth, after that has done for you Yahweh vengeances on your enemies, on [the] sons of Ammon.

en.L: And she said to him, "My father, you have opened your mouth to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; do to me according to what has gone out of your mouth, now that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done acts of vengeance for you on your enemies, on the sons of Ammon."
en.B: She said to him, "My father, you have given your word to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Do to me what you have promised, now that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought justice for you on your enemies the Ammonites."
en.R: She answered, "Father, you made a promise to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. So you must do to me what you said you would. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has punished your enemies, the Ammonites, for you."

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Baba yangu, umefungua kinywa chako kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; nitendee sawasawa na kile kilichotoka kinywani mwako, kwa kuwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekufanyia kisasi juu ya adui zako, juu ya wana wa Amoni."
sw.B: Alimwambia, "Baba yangu, umetoa ahadi kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Nitendee kama ulivyoahidi, kwa kuwa sasa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amekupatia haki juu ya adui zako Waamoni."
sw.R: Binti yake alijibu, "Baba, ulimwahidi {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Kwa hiyo lazima unitendee kama ulivyosema. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} amewaadhibu adui zako, Waamoni, kwa ajili yako."

es.L: Y ella le dijo: «Padre mío, has abierto tu boca {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}; haz conmigo conforme a lo que ha salido de tu boca, ya que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha hecho venganza por ti de tus enemigos, de los hijos de Amón».
es.B: Ella le dijo: «Padre mío, has dado tu palabra {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Haz conmigo lo que prometiste, ya que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} te ha hecho justicia contra tus enemigos los amonitas».
es.R: Ella le respondió: «Padre, le hiciste una promesa {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. Así que tienes que hacer conmigo lo que dijiste que harías. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} castigó a tus enemigos, los amonitas, por ti».

decisions.choice: acts of vengeance: the LORD's just punishment of Israel's enemies
decisions.reason: The word is not private revenge but the punishment a ruler or judge gives for a wrong. Jephthah asked the LORD, the Judge, to decide between Israel and Ammon (verse 27); the daughter sees the victory as his verdict.

decisions.choice: do to me according to what has gone out of your mouth: the vow must be kept
decisions.reason: She uses the words of the law on vows (Numbers 30:3) and accepts what her father has promised. She does not ask to be spared, only for time (verse 37).

decisions.choice: brought justice for you on / punished
decisions.reason: "Vengeance" in English often suggests personal revenge; Balanced and Readable use words that keep the sense of just punishment (m1).

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אָבִ֔יהָ יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לִּ֖י הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה הַרְפֵּ֨ה מִמֶּ֜נִּי שְׁנַ֣יִם חֳדָשִׁ֗ים וְאֵֽלְכָה֙ וְיָרַדְתִּ֣י עַל־הֶֽהָרִ֔ים וְאֶבְכֶּה֙ עַל־בְּתוּלַ֔י אָנֹכִ֖י וְרֵעוֹתָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to her father, let be done for me the thing the this: let me alone two months, and I will go and go down upon the mountains and weep over my virginity, I and my companions.

en.L: And she said to her father, "Let this thing be done for me: let me alone two months, that I may go and go down on the mountains and weep over my virginity, I and my companions."
en.B: She also said to her father, "Grant me this one request. Give me two months to go off into the hills with my friends and weep there, because I will never marry."
en.R: Then she said to her father, "Please do this one thing for me. Give me two months to go to the hills with my friends. I want to cry there because I will never get married and have children."

sw.L: Naye akamwambia baba yake, "Nifanyiwe jambo hili: niache miezi miwili, niende nishuke milimani nikaombolezee ubikira wangu, mimi na wenzangu."
sw.B: Pia alimwambia baba yake, "Nitimizie ombi hili moja. Nipe miezi miwili niende milimani pamoja na rafiki zangu nikalie huko, kwa sababu sitaolewa kamwe."
sw.R: Kisha alimwambia baba yake, "Tafadhali nifanyie jambo hili moja. Nipe miezi miwili niende milimani pamoja na rafiki zangu. Nataka kulia huko kwa sababu sitaolewa kamwe wala kuzaa watoto."

es.L: Y dijo a su padre: «Hágaseme esta cosa: déjame sola dos meses, y me iré y bajaré por los montes, y lloraré mi virginidad, yo y mis compañeras».
es.B: Y también le dijo a su padre: «Concédeme solo esto. Dame dos meses para irme a los montes con mis amigas y llorar allí, porque nunca me casaré».
es.R: Luego le dijo a su padre: «Por favor, haz esto por mí. Dame dos meses para ir a los montes con mis amigas. Quiero llorar allí, porque nunca me casaré ni tendré hijos».

decisions.choice: weep over my virginity: mourn that she will never marry or have children
decisions.reason: The word means the state of a young woman not yet married. To die, or to live, without marrying and bearing children was a great sorrow in Israel, and as an only child she would leave her father no descendants. She mourns what she will never have.

decisions.choice: go down upon the mountains: go off into the hill country
decisions.reason: "Go down" is unusual with "mountains"; it may mean going down from the town into the hill country around it. With one letter different the word would mean "roam", which fits well but is not what the text has.

decisions.choice: my companions: two spellings of one word
decisions.reason: The written text and the marginal reading tradition spell the word for "companions" slightly differently. Both mean her women friends; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: let me alone: leave me free for a while
decisions.reason: The verb means to let go or hold back. She asks for two months before the vow is carried out.

decisions.choice: weep, because I will never marry
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what weeping over her virginity means (m1); Literal keeps the phrase. They also leave the unusual "go down" as going off into the hills (m2).

decisions.choice: "lloraré mi virginidad" (L); "llorar ..., porque nunca me casaré" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew "weep over my virginity"; Balanced and Readable say what she mourns (m1): that she will never marry or have children, as the English does.

decisions.choice: he did to her his vow: he carried out what he had vowed
alternatives: he offered her as a burnt offering
he gave her to the LORD to live unmarried
decisions.reason: The narrator says only that Jephthah did what he had vowed, and the vow said that whoever came out would be the LORD's and be offered as a burnt offering (verse 31). The plain reading is that he put her to death as an offering, a deed the law condemns as the practice of the nations (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 12:31; 18:10; compare 2 Kings 3:27). Another reading holds that she was given to the LORD to live unmarried, perhaps serving at the sanctuary (compare Exodus 38:8; 1 Samuel 2:22). It points to the stress on her virginity in verses 37-39, to the possible "or" in verse 31, and to the lack of any mention of her death. Against it, the vow named a burnt offering, and the mourning and the yearly remembrance suit a death. The story reports the deed without praising it.

decisions.choice: she had not known a man: she had never had sexual relations
decisions.reason: "Know" is a common way of speaking of sexual union (Genesis 4:1). The words say she died, or lived on, without marriage or children (m1).

decisions.choice: it became a custom: the practice of verse 40
decisions.reason: The verb is feminine and could be read "she became an example" in Israel, but most naturally it means "it became a custom", which verse 40 then describes. The word is often used of a fixed law or rule.

decisions.choice: never had relations with a man / was still a virgin
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid the old English use of "know" for sexual union, which modern readers could misread (m2).

decisions.choice: did to her what he had vowed
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the narrator's plain, unexplained words, so that they do not settle the question that m1 leaves open.

decisions.choice: from days to days: year by year
decisions.reason: "Days" can mean a year's time; the phrase means every year, as in 1 Samuel 1:3.

decisions.choice: to commemorate: to tell her story and honor her
decisions.reason: The verb is rare. In 5:11 it means to tell or recount the LORD's deeds, so here it most likely means to retell and remember what happened to her. Some take it as "to lament", which would also suit the yearly gathering.

decisions.choice: went: a repeated, yearly practice
decisions.reason: The verb form describes something done again and again; the custom may still have been kept when the book was written.

decisions.choice: the young women of Israel
decisions.reason: "Daughters of Israel" here means the young women of the people, Jephthah's daughter's companions in age; Literal keeps "daughters".

decisions.choice: to tell the story ... and to remember her
decisions.reason: Readable gives both parts of what commemorating meant (m2).
